## Overview

Running a capable model on your own machine stopped being a hobbyist exercise, and the field moves faster than any book can follow. This one is written for that constraint: the method chapters cover inference parameters, hyperparameters, retrieval and evaluation, while the parts that age, such as benchmarks and product facts, are marked as an early-2026 snapshot with their sources.

It is one Quarto project rendered as **one book in two languages**, delivered as a readable site, a self-contained HTML file, a PDF, a DOCX and an EPUB.

## What is in it

- **Part I: Foundations**: why now, choosing a model
- **Part II: Running models**: ecosystem and install, Studio Chat, inference parameters
- **Part III: Training**: fine-tuning pipeline, hyperparameters, data recipes
- **Part IV: Developing and deploying**: export, coding agents, harnesses, Python, RAG cookbook, voice/vision/images, serving a team
- **Part V: Governing**: evaluation, GDPR and hardening, business case, strategy paper
- **Appendices**: researcher primer, sources and limits, projects directory, hardware guide, DPIA template

Every chapter also renders as a self-contained reveal deck with numbered, shareable URLs, plus its own PDF and HTML page. Companion code ships with each release: a fine-tuning script, an evaluation gate, a minimal RAG, an Ollama Modelfile. Chapter 3 embeds a WebLLM demo that runs in the browser with no install.

## How it is built

Chapters are bilingual source fragments (`::: {.en}` / `::: {.fr}`). A pre-render hook regenerates the merged book, the per-chapter documents and the project file from a single order file, so the table of contents cannot drift out of sync; a filter then selects the language, restores canonical heading ids and strips the bilingual speaker notes.

Slides and the book are deliberately separate documents: Quarto renders a document's HTML formats concurrently, and they race on the shared `_files` directory that self-contained slides depend on.

CI renders both languages on every push, publishes the site, attaches PDF/EPUB/DOCX to each `v*` release, and runs a monthly link-freshness audit that opens an issue when a chapter goes stale.
